 Baguio water utility assures sufficient water supply until next rainy season
 by 
 Liza Agoot
 Nov 16, 2026
 2:02 PM GMT+8
 SURE WATER. Baguio Water District General Manager Salvador Royeca assures consumers that the agency is implementing measures to prevent its water sources from drying up and ensure adequate supply until the next rainy season. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration has projected that the effects of El Niño will persist until March, followed by the summer season, prompting the agency to intensify water conservation efforts. (PNA file photo by Liza T. Agoot) 
 BAGUIO CITY – The Baguio Water District (BWD) has assured its consumers that available water sources will last until the next rainy season through water conservation measures and the implementation of various water harvesting systems.
 "We are expecting the worst, but we are giving the public an assurance that we will not allow our sources to dry up. We will have water for our needs until the next rainy season," BWD General Manager Salvador Royeca said Monday.
 Royeca said the agency has started implementing supply management measures in various areas to encourage residents to conserve water in their homes and properties.
 The measures include regulating water pressure and distribution schedules to prevent the depletion of aquifers and spring sources.
 "It is human nature that when we have little to use, we save. We have to do this so that we can encourage water saving, which is part of ensuring that our sources are properly managed. We have ample supply until March, which was projected to be the end of the El Niño, but it will be followed by the summer season," Royeca said in Filipino.
 He said the city benefited from the replenishment of underground water sources during the prolonged rains in August. Rainwater harvesting facilities also reached full capacity.
 The Santo Tomas rainwater harvesting facility alone has enough supply to last about six months, he added.
 Royeca said water rationing will also be implemented, with consumers receiving water at least twice every two weeks, unless other factors disrupt distribution.
 "With El Niño comes power shortage, and without power, our pumping stations will be affected," he said.
 To address possible power interruptions, BWD has purchased a mobile generator set as a backup power source.
 The agency also has eight water tankers that deliver water to consumers on a first-come, first-served basis. Additional tankers are expected to arrive following the ongoing procurement process.
 BWD charges PHP40 per drum of delivered water.
 Royeca encouraged residents to invest in water drums and other storage containers to ensure they have an adequate reserve at home.
 Long-term measures 
 Royeca said BWD has started implementing a 10-year plan to ensure a sustainable water supply throughout its franchise area.
 The plan includes drilling at least two underground water sources annually, investing in solar power for pumping stations and replacing old distribution lines to reduce leaks and nonrevenue water.
 BWD is also encouraging associations and organizations to adopt watersheds to help protect forest areas.
 Currently, 38 associations, organizations and corporations have adopted at least 500 square meters each of various watershed areas.
 "Our goal is to have at least 10 to 20 percent excess in production as part of the water sustainability goal," Royeca said.
 BWD currently produces an average of 55,000 cubic meters of water daily against a demand of 56,000 cubic meters. (PNA)
